You plan; StealthLab knows. 0) Once per repo, run the survey_repo prompt to write .stealth/claims.md (facts about this repo, each citing file:line). 1) find_ways(query, repo_claims=<claims.md text>) returns knowledge: the Goal, the chosen Procedure(s) with every step in full, alternatives, and which repo facts supported or blocked each choice. 2) You compile the plan into .stealth/procedures.md + .stealth/run.md yourself (the plan_and_run prompt has the format), then do each step or hand a one-line pointer to a subagent, and check each step's proof. 3) report_discovery(...) anything you had to fix or found a better way to do -- it's saved privately and comes back through stealth://procedures/{procedure_id}/claims next time. 4) If find_ways found no good way (or a clearly better one), submit_way(goal_id, ...) proposes yours for that Goal -- pick goal_id from find_ways' resolved or ambiguous candidates; it enters human review, it is never live or verified on submission. 5) Optional, to pick the cheapest model that will pass: recommend_models(procedure_id, candidates=["model|scaffold", ...]) returns a ladder (try A; if its check fails, B); after each attempt call report_model_run(...) with the returned instance_key so the per-goal model scores learn. Reads need no token; report_discovery, submit_way and report_model_run need a signed-in user or write token.

  3. Extract the imaginary components of the complex array.
  4. Calculate the mean of the imaginary components.
  5. Combine the real and imaginary means back into a single complex number.
